[R85] NEGATIVE - exact head e2f7c0c0ada3cce2a3ef7a9e895db6e58f54321f Independent review round R85-8 of PR #428 (issue #413), cleared context, all five lenses re-covered at this head. Reviewed in a fresh public clone detached at e2f7c0c0ada3cce2a3ef7a9e895db6e58f54321f (tree 5e4d4e29c4cf6f193ea89ac8f702c67d288b80bc), base 55518b470935f5478e0879bfc4ff183cc5d5ccc4 (the merge base with `dev`), ten commits on that base, the three public submodules at their pinned commits. The diff is `scripts/gen_toc.py`, `scripts/gen_toc_cases.py` (new) and `scripts/check_em_dash.py` and nothing else. One MAJOR, four MINOR, two SUGGESTIONs, no BLOCKER. `RTL` is banked at this head. `Conformance`, `Robustness`, `Tests` and `Docs` were applied and are not banked. **The termination claim does not hold.** Round 9 says every decision site either reads the renderer's class from `CLASSES` or refuses the page, and that the refusal holds what the reading does not. I measured that end to end through the shipped gate, against GitHub's renderer: 1. **The refusal applies only to the branch page.** The exemption is decided from the headings of the BASE page (`base_labels()`), which are walked with no refusal at all. So the refusal holds none of the three #440 sites it is said to hold. Worse, round 9 narrowed the type-1 and type-6 opener follow sets from `\s` (base and round 8) to space and tab, where the renderer reads space, tab, line tabulation and form feed. That narrowing turns four shapes the base gate and the round-8 gate REFUSED into exempt labels (F1, MAJOR). A two-line refusal of the base page closes all seven rows, and both self-tests still pass with it, so no arm holds that side. 2. **At the two type-1 closers the escape needs no refused character.** A blank inside `` stays exempt under any refusal, and so does a closing name Python's case fold matches: `re.IGNORECASE` matches U+017F to `s` and U+0131 to `i` (F2). 3. **The enumeration and its guard have blind spots.** They do not see an escaped code point in a pattern, an inline class, a character membership test, a call through an alias or a regex flag. A refusal site respelled with escapes is listed as `single source` with no note. Dropping `re.IGNORECASE` from either opener passes both self-tests and moves no tracked or fixture page, yet it reopens the escape for `
` interrupting a paragraph (F3). 4. **Two single-sourced classes are the wrong class for their position.** One is the opener follow set (F1). The other is the footnote label's stop class, which carries NUL although the renderer replaces NUL before any scanner reads the line. The round-8 gate refused that type-7 shape and this head exempts it (F4). So, plainly: **the refusal at the three #440 sites only looks as if it refuses.** It names the character and withholds provenance on the branch page. The page the label is copied from is never refused. Every round-8 finding (R85-7 F1 and F2, R86-8 F1 and F2) is CLOSED for the positions it named. Each is measured against the renderer and held by an arm that fails when the fix is reverted (table below). No tracked page at this head, at the base or at the live `dev` tip carries any shape named in this review, so nothing on the tree is affected today. ## What was read, and how the round was worked Read: issue #413 (objective, authority, acceptance 1 to 3), its parent #378 and PR #384 for the type-6 exclusion; #437 and #440; CONTRIBUTING.md 5, 6 and 6.1; AGENTS.md 6 and 7; docs/development/CODE_QUALITY.md rule 12; CommonMark 2.1 to 2.3, 4.5 and 4.6 (HTML block types 1, 6 and 7) and 6.6, from spec.txt in the public specification repository (review-evidence/commonmark/; NUL at :479-483, the closing fence at :1959-1960, type-1 start and end at :2375-2380, type 7 and paragraphs at :3047); the diff base..head and the round deltas 1c31ffb0..b7114c23..f593dc7c..aab51d49..e0c2fe08..e154f802..c67db0a5..2e86442d..e0315b19..e2f7c0c0. Also read: the PR description, which carries the round-9 report (no REVIEW READY comment exists for this head, S1); the validation record (comment 5651390751) and its replica appendix (5651634537); and the round-8 reviews R85-7 and R86-8, to judge closure. cmark-gfm's public source (review-evidence/cmark-gfm/) is cited only to explain what the renderer does. Every verdict rests on the renderer itself. Nothing below is taken from the author's evidence. Every figure comes from a tool written for this round, under `review-evidence/tools/` (index: `review-evidence/INDEX.txt`): - `oracle.py`: GitHub's Markdown rendering API in gfm mode as the oracle, every response cached (`oracle-cache/`), synthetic fixture text only. Each walk is loaded from a `git show` copy of the base, the round-8 head or this head (`mods/`) and called as `base_labels()` calls `headings()`. - `probe_sites.py`, `sweep_refused.py` (504 rows), `closure_probes.py` and a 46-row tag-grammar check: each page rendered alone. - `e2e_gate.py`: 15 shapes run through each revision's OWN gate, using that revision's `_fixture_git`, `_commit`, `_edit` and `judge`, plus the head's `_unwrap` verbatim so all three receive the same edit. Also run against a fix sketch on a copy. - `controls.py`: 17 bounded controls on the tracked `scripts/gen_toc.py`, one at a time, restored byte-exact and hashed after each. - `guard_mutants.py`, `mutant_reach.py`, `class_campaign.py`: single edits on copies (`mut/`), scored by the shipped guard and both self-tests, then measured for reach over 159 tracked pages, 228 fixture pages and renderer rows. - `dump_pages.py`: per-page answers of three walks over two page sets. ## Findings ```text [R85] MAJOR Conformance, Robustness, Tests, Docs - scripts/check_em_dash.py:210-217, :271-282; scripts/gen_toc.py:162-164, :182-184, :684 - the refusal is applied to the branch page only while the exemption is decided from the base page, walked unrefused, so it holds none of the positions it is said to hold, and this head exempts four shapes the base and round-8 gates refused Requirement/evidence: acceptance 1 of #413, and round 9's own construction. The PR body says a page carrying a refused character "is not walked at all ... it obtains no provenance, so no label copied from it can be exempt". gen_toc.py:96-101 says such a page is "REFUSED rather than walked (`refusals()`), which holds every position this file does not read the renderer's class at". gen_toc.py:287-289 says "it must not answer at all, and this is what stops it". The gate reads two pages to decide an exemption. Provenance comes from the BRANCH page: `generated_block(text, change.path)` (check_em_dash.py:282) answers None for a refused page (gen_toc.py:684), and the refusal note is added there too (:271-276). The label set comes from the BASE page: `base_labels()` (:210-217) runs `headings()` on `git show base:path`, applies no refusal, and is byte-identical to the base. A label is copied FROM the base page, and that is the page never refused. (a) The #440 sites. Each shape below ran end to end through the shipped gate. The base page carries the em-dash heading after the shape; the branch unwraps it and mirrors the label (the shape of the shipped `_unwrap` controls); GitHub renders no such heading at the base. The three shapes are a closing fence followed by a form feed (e2e row F1) or by a no-break space (row F2), and `` (row T3). Each reads `0 finding(s), 1 mirrored label(s) exempt` at this head, as at the base and round 8 (e2e-gate.txt). Over every refused character (sweep-refused.txt), 25 fence-closer rows and 25 type-1-closer rows are listed by the walk and hidden by the renderer, leaving out the carriage return, which both readers translate. `refusals()` names every one of them, on the branch side only. (b) A regression this head introduces. At the base and at round 8, RAW_HTML_OPEN_RE and HTML_BLOCK_OPEN_RE read `\s` after the tag name (patterns-r8-vs-head.txt). Here they read `blank`, which is space and tab. The renderer opens a type-1 or type-6 block on a space, a tab, a line tabulation, a form feed or a line end after the name (scanners.re:32, :178-189). render-samples.txt shows `` and `` rendering exactly as `
` and `
` do. CommonMark 0.31.2's prose says a
  space or a tab there (spec.txt:2375-2377); the PR names the renderer as
  the authority where the two differ, and the renderer reads wider.
  Four shapes through the gate: `Para.` + `` (O1), `x
` (O2), `` across a blank line (O3) and `Para.` + `` (O4). Each reads `1 finding(s) ... mirrors no heading` at the base and at round 8, and `0 finding(s), 1 mirrored label(s) exempt` at this head. In the sweep, eight rows (P01 to P04, each with a line tabulation and a form feed) agree at the base and escape here. No arm pins the narrowing: reading the renderer's class at either opener (controls C03, C04) passes 267/267 and 33/33. (c) No arm can see it. The seven refusal arms score `refusals()`, `refusal_notes()` and `generated_block()` (gen_toc_cases.py:857-887). The gate's new control plants its no-break space in the branch page (check_em_dash.py:718-728). A two-line sketch that also refuses the base page (`if refusal_notes(change.base_path, text): return set()` in `base_labels()`, e2e/fixsketch.diff) turns e2e rows F1, F2, T3 and O1 to O4 into refusals, and still passes `PASS (33 arm(s))` and `PASS (267/267 arm(s))`. Reach: 0 of 159 pages carry any of the 26 characters at this head, at the base and at the dev tip a86247fb (reach.txt). Impact: this is the escape #413 exists to close, reachable through the shipped gate at every position the refusal is said to hold. For the type-1 and type-6 exclusions #384 landed it is also a regression: this head exempts a label its base refused. The construction meant to end the review loop exempts whatever divergence a later reader finds in a base page, instead of refusing it. Required change: a page the walk refuses decides no exemption on either side it is read on. That means the base page whose headings decide the label as well as the branch page whose block decides provenance. An arm must plant a refused character in the base page only and fail when that refusal is removed. O1 to O4 must be refused again; a base-side refusal does it, and so does reading the renderer's class at the two openers. The statements quoted above must say what is enforced. Verification: review-evidence/tools/e2e_gate.py rows F1, F2, T3 and O1 to O4 read refused at the new head; sweep_refused.py rows P01 to P06 agree or are refused through the base page; removing the base-side refusal fails an arm. ``` ```text [R85] MINOR Robustness, Docs - scripts/gen_toc.py:462, :489; gen_toc.py:96-101; PR #428 body, Known limitations and the acceptance-1 statement - at the two type-1 closers the escape needs no refused character, so no refusal holds it: a blank inside ``, and a closing name Python's case fold matches Requirement/evidence: the PR says the #440 sites are where "the refusal, not a reading, is what stops the escape" and that they are "held meanwhile by the refusal". gen_toc.py:96-101 names "the fence and type-1 closers #440 carries" among the positions the refusal holds. The renderer ends a type-1 block only on a line containing the literal ``, ``, `` or ``, case-insensitive in ASCII only (spec.txt:2378-2380; scanners.re:204-212). The walk ends it on `` with `re.IGNORECASE` (:462, and :489 on the opening line). Two things there are not whitespace divergences at all. One is the space and tab that `\s*` admits, where the renderer admits nothing inside the tag. The other is Python's Unicode case folding, under which `s` matches U+017F and `i` matches U+0131 and U+0130. Through the shipped gate (e2e-gate.txt), these stay exempt at the base, at round 8, at this head and under the base-side sketch: `` (T1), `` (T2), `
x
` (T6), `` (T4) and `` (T5). GitHub renders no such heading (render-samples.txt). In the probe (probe-sites.txt A2, A3, B1 to B3), 4 blank rows and 6 fold rows answer identically at the base, so this change widens nothing here. #440 counts the space and tab rows among its 27 but describes the class as "the same 25"; the fold rows are in no issue. Impact: the escape direction at the type-1 closers, which the declaration says is held and is not. Required change: no change to the reading in this lane (it is #440's). The statements must say that the refusal does not hold a blank inside a type-1 closing tag or a case-folded closing name, each with its direction, and the fold rows must be recorded beside #440's. Verification: every statement about the #440 sites matches e2e rows T1, T2 and T4 to T6; #440 or a successor names both row families. ``` ```text [R85] MINOR Tests, Docs - scripts/gen_toc.py:798-880 (`_class_guards`), :164, :184 (`re.IGNORECASE`), :63-66; scripts/gen_toc_cases.py:769-771, :795-847, :301-304 - the enumeration and its guard close the family only for the spellings they read, the case-fold flag no table entry owns is held by no arm, and the class table is held by its literal copy rather than by behaviour Requirement/evidence: round 9 claims that "a site added with a class of its own fails an arm" and that the family is "closed by construction". `_class_guards()` lists what it cannot see as "a class reached through getattr, built at run time or imported ... as does a rule the walk never calls". Each edit below was applied to a copy of the scripts directory (review-evidence/mut/), or to the tracked file where marked, and scored by the shipped guard and both self-tests. (a) Spellings the guard does not refuse (guard-mutants.txt): - M01: a type-1 closer's `\s*` respelled as `[\x20\x09\x0b\x0c]*`. - M02: the fence closer's bare strip respelled as `re.sub(r"[\x20\x09\x0b\x0c]", ...)`. Both M01 and M02 are listed as `single source` where `--sites` said `refusal`, with no note. - M03: the ordinal class spelled inline; `[.)]` already ships inline at :229. - M04: `_indent_columns()`'s class spelled as a literal in a membership test. - M05: `_table_cells()` called through a local alias. That drops two sites from the enumeration (26 to 24, and no arm pins the count) and hides a literal strip inside it. - M06: HEAD_RE's blanks respelled with escapes, with a form feed added. Every one passes `PASS (267/267 arm(s))` and `PASS (33 arm(s))`. M06 lists `##\fTarget`, a heading GitHub does not render (mutant-reach.txt). None of these is getattr, run time, an import or a function the walk never calls. (b) The flag. Dropping `re.IGNORECASE` from the type-6 opener (C05) or the type-1 opener (C06), on the tracked file and restored, passes 267/267 and 33/33 and draws no note. The mutants escape on `Para.` + `
